_note: Tavern nights (Curtis, 26 November 2026). A night opens when the party finishes one of the chapters below (or a job trial, or the last written chapter), and closes when the party next sets out on an expedition. The tavern only opens its door to a party with an empty place (fewer than three companions, someone away for a chapter still counting). Each night offers 2 or 3 people picked at random from the roster (src/data/tavern-roster.json); whoever is offered and not hired moves on for good once the party has been in and set out again. Declining Nessa keeps its cost: there is no night before the Oath of the Road at level 10, a hire costs a fee by level, fights a little below a story companion, has no personal quest, and never takes Nessa's place. src/tavern.js builds the nodes; lines use the scene format, and 'offered'/'tavernSeen' in a line's when follow tonight's offer.

lines.narrate: Highpass does what it always does with an oath: it drinks to it. The inn's taproom is packed to the rafters with roadwardens, and every one of them wants to shake the hand that swore it. Someone has pinned a notice by the door in a careful, upright hand: THE COMPANY OF THE OATH IS ONE SHORT. ENQUIRE WITHIN.

lines.text: I did. It was true, and the guild lent me a pen.

lines.narrate: The harbour bell rang true tonight, and Merrowgate's dockside taproom has decided that this is everyone's business. Fishermen are buying drinks for sailors they were punching last week. Maren's notice is pinned by the door again, a little damper than the last one.

Word of your Second Oath has gone round Cinder Fold before you have finished washing. In the inn's taproom the forge-hands have pushed two tables together for you, and the notice has followed you up the mountain.

lines.text: It's a big oath. It wants more than three people holding it.

lines.narrate: You came home to Briarwatch for help, and Briarwatch has given what it could: bread, beds, a cart, and the inn's taproom for as long as you need it. The notice by the door is in a child's hand this time, copied out large: HELP WANTED. BRAVE PREFERRED.

The winter watch is over and Briarwatch has come in out of the snow. The taproom smells of wet wool and mulled cider. Tomorrow the road goes down to Vell and does not come back up until it is done. Tonight the notice by the door is still asking.

lines.text: Last night anyone can join us. After this it's the stair.

lines.narrate: Somebody in the taproom is singing the song about you again, the version with the extra verse, and the whole room comes in on the chorus. The notice by the door has been up so long that someone has added a line underneath in pencil: ASK FOR THE ONE IN THE SONG.

lines.text: The song gets my hammer wrong.

lines.narrate: It is a quiet night in Briarwatch, the first in a long while, and the taproom is half empty and glad of it. The fire is low. The notice is still by the door, curling at the corners.

lines.text: Nobody's going to answer that now.

books.title: The First Night of Your Own Story

lines.narrate: The written road is behind you. What comes next is yours to make, and the inn's taproom is as good a place to start as any: warm, loud, and full of people who would like to be in a story. The notice is pinned by the door.
Word of the trial travels faster than you do. By the time you reach the inn the taproom has heard three versions of it, and two of them have dragons. The notice is by the door, where it always is.
By the second round, a few people have answered the notice.

lines.text: We turned one away on a bench in Briarwatch.
We did. That doesn't mean we have to keep doing it.

lines.narrate: The same faces are still here, waiting to see what you decide.

lines.text: Any of them is more than we've got.
They'd be hired, not sworn. They'll fight for us. Whether they'll stay for us is another thing.

tavern.hireDescription: {kindWord}, {roleLower}. {summary} Fee: {total} gold now ({fee} for each of your levels). The others will move on.

hiredAfter.narrate: The others finish their drinks and wish you a safe road. By the next time you are through, they will have moved on.

leave.label: Not tonight
leave.description: Keep the party as it is. They will wait tonight, until you next set out; after that they move on, and the tavern opens again only at another turn in the story, with other faces.

lines.narrate: You finish your drink and leave the notice where it is.
